input:
CURRENT SCENE:
很久以前，古代的人很不知道什么植物能吃，也什么植物不能吃。所以很多人常常吃不安全的植物，吃不安全的植物对你的身体有坏处，很麻烦的情况。但是一个人，神农，要解决这个问题。

ITEMS:

[I156] 古代的人【很】不知道什么植物能吃   correction: 很 → (delete)   strength: error
  checker's note: 很 cannot modify 不知道 here
  rule card (fixed_expressions, Vocabulary): Use established fixed expressions and compounds, rather than literal or self-created word combinations. For example, use 自然规律, 制定规定, and 从 + Place.  Pattern: <wrong> → <correct>: use the established expression <correct>, not the literal/nonstandard combination <wrong>.  Her terms: 从 + Place, 制定规定, 自然规律, Subj.算是Obj., 只/不过/才(+num.) + 而已
  her past correction: 在古代[-时候]中国人不知道什么植物可以吃
  her past correction: 神农发现[-了]大家都不知道什么植物能吃 — her note: 发现is a mental state verb, no了
  her past correction: 古代的生活很多的人吃很多[-的]植物

[I157] 也【^】什么植物不能吃   correction: ∅ → 不知道   strength: error
  checker's note: parallel clause needs the verb 不知道
  rule card (question_patterns, Grammar): Use 是……吗, V不V, or a Wh-question for an indirect question, not 如果. For “wh-ever…, will do that…”, repeat the Wh-word: 哪一筐……就……哪一筐.  Pattern: <wrong> → <correct>: this asks <whether/what/where>, so use <question pattern>, not 如果.  Her terms: repeated Wh-Q
  her past correction: 他们不知道什么植物[-能吃]不能吃
  her past correction: 每个人都不知道哪些植物能安全[+地]吃
  her past correction: [因为→这样]大家知道什么植物不能吃 — her note: not “because”

[I158] 也什【么】植物不能吃   correction: 么 → 麼   strength: suggestion
  rule card (cause_result_soyi, Coherence: connectors): Use 所以 only when the clause before it gives the cause/reason and the clause after it is the result. If there is no cause-result relationship, delete 所以 or use a connector such as 这样, 后来, or 结果 when appropriate.  Pattern: <wrong> → <correct>: the following event is not a result of the preceding clause, so 所以 is not appropriate; use <connector> / delete it.  Her terms: 这样, 结果, 后来
  her past correction: [因为→这样]大家知道什么植物不能吃 — her note: not “because”
  her past correction: 他们不知道什么植物[-能吃]不能吃
  her past correction: 但是不多植物[可能→不能]吃

[I159] 所以很多人常常吃【不安全】的植物   correction: 不安全 → 有毒   strength: suggestion
  checker's note: plants harmful to eat are usually called 有毒的
  rule card (modifier_de_structure, Grammar): Use 的 after a modifier when it describes a noun, especially a longer phrase such as 人类创造的文明 or 能吃的植物. Do not add 的 after quantity words or fixed modifiers where it is not needed, such as 很多人, 一些人, 今天清晨, 蓝色衣服, and 好主意.  Pattern: <wrong> → <correct>: <modifier> describes the noun <noun>, so use 的; or <modifier> does not need 的 here, so omit it.  Her terms: no的
  her past correction: 他们吃[毒→有毒的]植物
  her past correction: 很多的人吃了有毒的[饭→植物]
  her past correction: 哪些植物是[毒→有毒]

[I160] 所以很多人常常吃不安全的【植】物   correction: 植 → 食   strength: suggestion
  rule card (modifier_de_structure, Grammar): Use 的 after a modifier when it describes a noun, especially a longer phrase such as 人类创造的文明 or 能吃的植物. Do not add 的 after quantity words or fixed modifiers where it is not needed, such as 很多人, 一些人, 今天清晨, 蓝色衣服, and 好主意.  Pattern: <wrong> → <correct>: <modifier> describes the noun <noun>, so use 的; or <modifier> does not need 的 here, so omit it.  Her terms: no的
  her past correction: 很多的人吃了有毒的[饭→植物]
  her past correction: 吃很多[-的]植物
  her past correction: 每个人都不知道哪些植物能安全[+地]吃

[I161] 吃【不安全】的植物对你的身体有坏处   correction: 不安全 → 有毒   strength: error
  checker's note: plants harmful to eat are usually called 有毒的
  rule card (modifier_de_structure, Grammar): Use 的 after a modifier when it describes a noun, especially a longer phrase such as 人类创造的文明 or 能吃的植物. Do not add 的 after quantity words or fixed modifiers where it is not needed, such as 很多人, 一些人, 今天清晨, 蓝色衣服, and 好主意.  Pattern: <wrong> → <correct>: <modifier> describes the noun <noun>, so use 的; or <modifier> does not need 的 here, so omit it.  Her terms: no的
  her past correction: 他们吃[毒→有毒的]植物
  her past correction: 哪些植物对[-你的]健康有好处
  her past correction: 哪些植物是[毒→有毒]

[I162] 吃不安全的【植物】对你的身体有坏处   correction: 植物 → 食品   strength: suggestion
  rule card (specific_noun_choice, Vocabulary): Use a specific noun or noun phrase when the story needs to say exactly what person, thing, plant, experience, or problem you mean. Avoid general words such as 人、东西、事情、水果, or vague phrases such as 有麻烦.  Pattern: <wrong> → <correct>: <wrong> is too general/vague here; say specifically what <person/thing/problem> it is.
  her past correction: 很多的人吃了有毒的[饭→植物]
  her past correction: 没有人知道什么[食品→植物]能吃 — her note: “食品” is usually for processed food
  her past correction: 哪些植物对[-你的]健康有好处

[I163] 吃不安全的植物对【你的】身体有坏处   correction: 你的 → 人的   strength: error
  checker's note: generic statement should not shift to you
  rule card (possessive_reference, Coherence: reference): Do not use 他的/她的 for people or a place when it sounds like the person owns them. Use a precise relationship word, such as 家人, 朋友邻居, 人们, or 这个小城市.  Pattern: <wrong> → <correct>: <他的/她的 + noun> implies that <person> owns <noun>; use <relationship/reference expression> instead.
  her past correction: 哪些植物对[-你的]健康有好处
  her past correction: [-这些植物]对身体好处
  her past correction: 每个人都不知道哪些植物能安全[+地]吃

[I164] 【^】很麻烦的情况   correction: ∅ → 这是一个   strength: error
  checker's note: the noun phrase needs a subject and verb
  rule card (collocation_selection, Vocabulary): Use words with their normal collocations: a word must naturally match the noun, person, thing, action, or situation it describes. A grammatically possible combination may still sound unnatural in Chinese.  Pattern: <wrong> → <correct>: <word/expression> does not normally collocate with <noun/action/situation>; use <correct> instead.  Her terms: Time + 期间, V.得很厉害, 着durative, no了for habit/routine
  her past correction: 很多的东西⟦麻烦得很⟧ — her note: 麻烦is usually not used to describe植物
  her past correction: 先打了[+个]大哈欠
  her past correction: 但是什么时候都太吵了[+那儿]

[I165] 但是【^】一个人   correction: ∅ → 有   strength: error
  checker's note: introducing a new person needs 有
  rule card (verb_object_valency, Grammar): Use the verb structure that the verb allows: give it the needed object, and do not add an extra object after a V.+Obj. compound or complement. For example, 跑遍 + place, while 掉 cannot take an object by itself.  Pattern: <wrong> → <correct>: <verb/verb phrase> must take <the allowed object or complement structure>; <brief reason, such as “it is a V.+Obj. compound” or “the action is durative, so use 着durative”>.  Her terms: 着durative, 跑遍 + place, 管事V.+Obj. compound, 掉 + directional + place, resultative complement
  her past correction: 因为他怕[+有]毒
  her past correction: [+但]据人类法律规定
  her past correction: 先打了[+个]大哈欠

[I166] 【神农】   correction: (comment, no correction)   strength: error
  checker's note: first appearance of 神农: briefly introduce who this is
  rule card (first_mention_introduction, Coherence: reference): When a character first appears, briefly introduce the person with an identifying noun phrase, not only a name or pronoun. The first appearing noun should not be specific.  Pattern: <name/pronoun> → <brief introduction to the person>: this character appears for the first time, so please introduce <person> briefly.
  her past correction: 这是一个⟦神农⟧的古代故事 — her note: better to briefly introduce “神农” when this character first appears
  her past correction: ⟦神农⟧是很聪明的人 — her note: better to briefly introduce “神农” when this character first appears
  her past correction: 所以⟦神农⟧去旅行 — her note: better to briefly introduce “神农” when this character first appears

items.explanation: 很 cannot modify 不知道 here. Say 不知道什么植物能吃.
The two parts are parallel: 不知道什么植物能吃，也不知道什么植物不能吃. Repeat 不知道 in the second part.
It would be more natural to write 什麼 with the traditional character 麼.
It would be more natural to say 有毒的植物. Plants that are harmful to eat are usually called 有毒的.
It would be more natural to say 食物 for things people eat.
Use the established expression 有毒的植物, not 不安全的植物, for plants that harm people when eaten.
It would be more natural to say 食品 here to refer specifically to things people eat.
This is a general statement about people, so use 人的身体, not 你的身体.
很麻烦的情况 is only a noun phrase. Add 这是一个 to make it a complete sentence: 这是一个很麻烦的情况.
Use 有 to introduce a new person: 但是有一个人.
神农 appears for the first time here, so briefly introduce him with an identifying phrase, not only his name.
